ALISON SOSEBEE.name: B Alison Sosebee
ALISON SOSEBEE.background: Barbara Alison Sosebee, a lifelong Fannin County resident from Blue Ridge; daughter of Robert L. Sosebee Sr. (former general manager of Tri-State Electric Cooperative) and Barbara Payne Sosebee; mother of two sons. Bachelor's degree and J.D. from the University of Georgia. Law clerk to Chief Judge Brenda Weaver (2001), associate in the law office of George W. Weaver, then sole practitioner in Blue Ridge (B. Alison Sosebee, P.C.); also served as juvenile court judge pro tem for the Appalachian Circuit, city attorney for East Ellijay and city attorney/solicitor for McCaysville, and solicitor, public defender and judge pro tem of the Ellijay Municipal Court. Won the 2012 Republican primary for Appalachian Judicial Circuit (Fannin, Gilmer, Pickens) District Attorney over incumbent Joe Hendricks and former superior court judge Harry Doss; took office January 2013; re-elected unopposed in 2016 and 2020. Appointed by Gov. Brian Kemp on Dec. 27, 2023 to the Appalachian Circuit Superior Court seat left vacant by the death of Judge John Worcester; sworn in January 2024. Elected unopposed to that seat in the May 19, 2026 nonpartisan election (18,506 votes).
ALISON SOSEBEE.ideology: Elected district attorney as a Republican (2012, 2016, 2020); her judicial seat is nonpartisan. No outlet or rating placed her ideologically. On taking office in 2013 she said supporters wanted change in the DA's office and that her priority was justice; she later pledged that each case would be "evaluated on its merits."
ALISON SOSEBEE.record: District Attorney of the Appalachian Judicial Circuit, January 2013 to January 2024. Reorganized the office on arrival (new chief investigator Greg Arp, full review of pending cases). Chaired the control board of the Zell Miller Mountain Pathway Drug Task Force (name as given in the Governor's release) and sat on the Cherokee Multi-Agency Narcotics Squad and Appalachian Regional Drug Enforcement Office control boards; served on the circuit's sexual-assault and child-abuse protocol committees; member of the District Attorneys' Association of Georgia. As her first act as a superior court judge she swore in her successor as DA, Frank Wood. Her appointment made the Appalachian Circuit the only one in Georgia with three female superior court judges.
ALISON SOSEBEE.notes: Ballot name 'B Alison Sosebee'; full name Barbara Alison Sosebee (Branch Politics). All races under this name are the same person: Appalachian Circuit DA (R) 2016 and 2020, unopposed both times, then Superior Court (Sosebee seat) 2026 after her December 2023 appointment. The News Observer says she was 'first elected in 2013'; FetchYourNews (2016) says she won the 2012 primary and was sworn in for her first term in January 2013. Use: elected 2012, took office 2013. The Governor's release has a typo calling her 'Benton' in one sentence and gives the task force as 'Zell Miller Mountain Pathway Drug Task Force'; that spelling is kept here, but verify the task force's exact name before publishing.
